sources.source_updated_at: The BMS's goal is to govern the flow of energy to and from the battery system, monitoring sensor data with computational methods to identify events indicating degradation, as well as initiate self-healing actions. The resulting solution will revamp the European sector of rechargeable batteries with high round-trip efficiency energy storage for numerous applications, as specified in the EU Green Deal, consequently promoting innovative ideas needed to develop future sustainable batteries which demand fewer resources and create the groundwork for EU competitiveness. The project will be aligned with the Battery2030+ large-scale initiative within their ""Integration of smart functionalities"" theme, which supports sensing and self-healing.""

mechanism.zh: Horizon Europe创新行动。项目期为2022-05-01至2026-04-30；欧盟最高资助额为9.79百万欧元，登记总成本为12.32百万欧元。
mechanism.en: Horizon Europe IA; 2022-05-01 to 2026-04-30. Maximum EU contribution EUR 9.79 million; registered total cost EUR 12.32 million.

observed.zh: 官方登记技术目标：建设电池拆解与湿法冶金两套中试系统，目标包括回收95%的电池包组件，以及从黑粉中分离石墨、铝、铜和锰；同时开发电池维修、梯次利用与原料追溯流程。
observed.en: Registered technical objectives: Recycling of end of life battery packs for domestic raw material supply chains and enhanced circular economy

objective_excerpt.en: BATRAW main objective is to develop and demonstrate two innovative pilot systems for sustainable recycling and end of life management of EV batteries, domestic batteries, and battery scraps contributing to the generation of secondary streams of strategically important CRMs and battery RMs. The first pilot will deliver innovative technologies and processes for dismantling of battery packs achieving recovery of 95% of battery pack components and separating waste streams including cells and modules by semi-automated processes for recycling. BATRAW's second pilot will scale and demonstrate efficient pre-treatment and continuous hydrometallurgical recycling of battery cells and modules including innovative steps for C-graphite, Al and Cu separation from black mass and Mn extraction, achieving a recovery of the full range of battery RMs (Co, Ni, Mn, Li, C-graphite, Al and Cu) at selectivity of 90-98%. Innovations wil be scaled and demonstrated in a pilot systems with recycling capacity of 1 ton lithium-ion battery (LIB) packs dismantled per shift (8 hours) and treat 300 kg BM per day. BATRAW outcomes are of strategic importance within the prospects of the exponentially growing EU battery market and reducing EU import dependency of CRMs. The project will further promote the overall sustainability and circularity of battery products and raw materials by developing new procedures for battery repair and reuse, enabling faster diagnostics and conversion of EV packs into second life batteries, delivering eco-design guidelines for battery manufacturing,  demonstrating blockchain platform for raw material tracking and supply chain transparency (Battery Passport) and delivering guidelines for safe transports and handling of battery waste. The project aims to maximize market uptake and impact through ambitious C&D&E plan including circular business models, innovations workshops, dissemination in EU platforms, policy briefs and other strategies to reach markets and stakeholders.

objective_excerpt.en: To prevent the worst outcomes of climate change and increase Europe’s energy independence, urgent and massive efforts are required to transform Europe’s energy production to renewable and secure sources. Photovoltaics (PV) has emerged as a key technology in these efforts with projected annual growth rates of 30-35% over the next years. A strong base of PV industry across the entire value chain is, therefore, of strategic importance for Europe to support this strong market growth.Since the currently dominating silicon (Si) PV technology is approaching its efficiency limit, PEPPERONI aims to 'spice up' cost-efficient industrial Si cells with a thin perovskite top cell in a monolithic tandem device. This technology promises the best ratio of performance over manufacturing costs and therefore enables to push solar module efficiencies beyond the limit of Si at lowest CO2 footprint.The key objective of PEPPERONI is to enable large-scale production of such tandem PV modules in Europe by (i) demonstrating 26%-efficient modules on industrial scale; (ii) developing fabrication processes for high-volume manufacturing; (iii) extending the operational stability of tandems to meet market expectations (>30 yr); and (iv) removing any human health or environmental risk.To reach these objectives, PEPPERONI capitalises on the world-leading tandem PV expertise of a strong and complementary consortium: 4 equipment suppliers, 2 material suppliers, 1 service provider, 9 R&D institutes and universities that hold tandem efficiency world records, and one of the world's largest PV module manufacturers: PEPPERONI coordinator Q CELLS. When joining forces, their excellence puts PEPPERONI in the unique position to set up a tandem pilot line in Europe by 2026. This will establish a robust and competitive European innovation base and PV supply chain, putting all involved partners well on track towards GW-scale production of solar modules in Europe by 2030.

objective_excerpt.en: CLEANHYPRO gathers some of the most recognised experts in Europe on the electrolysis field for clean hydrogen production and acknowledged facilitators of technology transfer, corporate finance, funding and coaching, making available (i) the most promising and breakthrough manufacturing pilots and (ii) advanced characterization techniques and modelling together with (iii) non-technical services through this Test Bed: while relevant improvement metrics can be defined, the potential network of reachable stakeholders counts thousands of businesses on an international scale. Key facts are reported below. Within the scope of CLEANHYPRO, several circular innovative materials and key components, four main electrolysis technologies and geometries will be covered, providing for the first time a single entry point for industrial partners, mainly SMEs, aspiring to answer their concerns but with minimum investment costs and reduction of risks associated with technology transfer, while opening-up opportunities for demonstration of materials and components (TRL7) and thus faster opening the market for these new products. The main KPIs for CLEANHYPRO: Technical: >20% cell productivity improvement, 30% faster verification, 27-58% and 22-79% cost reduction of technologies in CAPEX and OPEX respectively, 3-9% efficiency enhancement. Non-Technical: 4 Showcases, 4 certification schemes, ≥16 Democases, >100 reachable SMEs and > 300 reachable investors. INNOMEM stems from the consideration that the development of products based on key materials and components for electrolysis require access to finance and an optimised business planning, relying on a sound prior analysis of the market, of the economic impacts and capacity of a company. The project aims at developing and organizing a sustainable Open Innovation Test Bed (OITB) for electrolysis materials and components for different applications. The OITB will also offer a network of facilities and services through a SEP to companies.

objective_excerpt.en: The Icarus consortium has identified critical technology steps that at present limit the wider deployment of three Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) production routes, namely: biocrude from hydrothermal liquefaction to SAF, isobutanol from lignocellulosic biomass to SAF and synthetic Fischer-Tropsh from biomass gasification to SAF. These three value chains have been strategically selected by Icarus since they are close to market deployment and are needed to meet European and international SAF deployment targets. Icarus aims to improve them with innovative solutions while at the same time addressing the whole value chain. Novel biomass production concepts such as sequential cropping and mix cropping are also addressed aiming to ensure increased sustainable biomass availability for SAF production. Along the complete value chain techno-economic, environmental, and social assessments will be carried out. Icarus has a very strong international consortium of 20 reputed partners including 5 from 3 Mission Innovation Countries (MIC) Canada, India and Brazil, who will carry out innovative research with common targets and objectives with the European ones ensuring international collaboration in this critical area. Two more partners from a 4th MIC, USA are joining research activities as members of the External Executive Advisory Board (EEAB). The Icarus results will significantly improve the cost effectiveness of SAF and therefore have global significance and reach and will facilitate scaling-up of these technologies and value chains enabling market deployment of SAF on a global scale. Guidelines, assessments, best practices and improved concepts will be used throughout the project to disseminate the results on global scale via targeted and effective dissemination and communication outreach activities to all stakeholders.

summary.zh: 由Centria协调，连接电池健康与安全状态表征、人工智能自动拆解、DHL参与的逆向物流以及区块链电池护照和交易平台。目标是使退役电池在维修、再使用、再制造和回收之间按状态分流；福特参与电动交通应用衔接。 联合体包括7个国家的11家机构，其中企业9家、高校及研究机构2家；欧盟最高资助额4.90百万欧元。

Combining these advances with a blockchain-based platform, that will combine the data collected during dismantling and recycling and the battery provenance, will enable a unique battery passport and virtual marketplace for e-mobility, consumer and stationary Battery Energy Storage Systems. observed.zh: 官方登记技术目标：由Centria协调，连接电池健康与安全状态表征、人工智能自动拆解、DHL参与的逆向物流以及区块链电池护照和交易平台。目标是使退役电池在维修、再使用、再制造和回收之间按状态分流；福特参与电动交通应用衔接。
observed.en: Registered technical objectives: Reuse of batteries through characterisation, smart logistics, automated pack and module dismantling and repackaging and a blockchain enabled marketplace.

objective_excerpt.en: RECIRCULATE addresses the needs of European recycling sector by overcoming current challenges relating to automated dismantling and sorting; safe logistics; fast, cost-effective and reliable State of Health and State of Safety characterization. Combining these advances with a blockchain-based platform, that will combine the data collected during dismantling and recycling and the battery provenance, will enable a unique battery passport and virtual marketplace for e-mobility, consumer and stationary Battery Energy Storage Systems. This approach will enable the RECIRCULATE consortium to create a cascade approach that will enable increased end-of-life battery repair, reuse, remanufacture and recycling.The advances in RECIRCULATE will based on best-in-world innovations, including:•Automated dismantling based on Artificial Intelligence with accurate sorting by SoX and battery provenance for recycling.•Fast, cost-effective, reliable SoX characterization; Safe storage and transportation based on smart logistics solutions.•Blockchain-based Battery Passports that tracks key battery data, and enables both a complete circular system for e-mobility batteries and a unique, blockchain-based virtual marketplace.The unique virtual marketplace will allow for the creation of new circular business models for repair, reuse, remanufacture and recycling of second-life batteries, minimizing cost, time, energy and environmental impact whilst maximizing battery value.RECIRCULATE represents a pan-European consortium of world leading organisations that are looking to commercialize these technologies of European origin. The coordinator, Centria, is leading activities in battery dismantling. The consortium is strengthened by very large organisations, including: Ford, who are currently undertaking development for e-mobility, and DHL a global leader in logistics and reverse logistics as well as European SMEs with world leading technologies.

summary.zh: 电池企业、追溯服务商与供应链伙伴试验产品级可持续性数据采集，探索电池护照的规则与验证。
summary.en: Battery firms, traceability providers and supply-chain partners pilot product-level sustainability data collection and passport verification.

actors.zh: 全球电池联盟、试点联合体、电芯制造商、数字追溯服务商及供应链企业。
actors.en: GBA, pilot consortia, cell manufacturers, traceability providers and supply-chain firms.

mechanism.zh: 使用多方制定的规则采集数据并形成原型护照，以试验识别数据完整性、验证及互操作问题。
mechanism.en: Multistakeholder rules guide data collection and prototype passports, revealing completeness, verification and interoperability issues.

observed.zh: 2024年试点由10个联合体形成原型护照；报告同时指出不同追溯系统互操作性未在该轮测试，试点评分不可直接跨组比较。
observed.en: Ten consortia produced prototype passports in the 2024 pilots; the report notes untested inter-provider interoperability and non-comparable pilot scores.

constraints.zh: 这是数据治理探索而非成熟的统一认证。商业保密、供应链负担与验证口径仍需处理。
constraints.en: This is a governance pilot, not a mature universal certification; confidentiality, supplier burdens and verification conventions remain important.

transfer.zh: 推进产业数据平台时，先统一指标定义与证据要求，再测试跨平台交换，不以展示二维码替代可信数据。
transfer.en: Align indicators and evidence requirements before testing cross-platform exchange; a QR code cannot substitute for trustworthy data.

objective_excerpt.en: HyWay aims to develop adaptive multiscale material modelling and characterisation suites for assessing interactions between hydrogen and advanced metallic materials and demonstrate their capabilities on hydrogen storage and transport components.Advanced materials application like hydrogen technologies is essential for achieving the EU carbon neutrality goal. However, deploying hydrogen technologies needs a tremendous effort to complete the infrastructure, requiring efficient material assessment suites, enabling industries to be more effective in developing and working with materials. Furthermore, since hydrogen is stored and transported in several forms, the material assessment suites must be flexible and capable of revealing hydrogen-material interactions in various conditions.The HyWay suites contain 3 key modules: Physical realm, Virtual world, and Data and knowledge management platform (DKMP). The Physical realm will advance experimental capabilities to reveal hydrogen-material interactions by compiling characterisation methodologies across length scales. The Virtual world will develop a multiscale and multiphysics materials modelling framework for disclosing how hydrogen alters changes in advanced materials under various service conditions. The Physical realm and the Virtual world are interdependent and complement each other through the data exchange between modules. We will establish the DKMP to facilitate the data exchange and merge material research disciplines.HyWay will ensure the productive allocation of investments required in constructing the hydrogen infrastructure. We will strengthen European capability in steering green transition with digital technologies and future emerging enabling technologies and ensure an open strategic autonomy by supporting the transformation of the EU energy mix to be dominated by hydrogen. The consortium comprises renowned experts from academia and industries across the EU and will support Ukraine on its European path.

FLEXIndustries develops and demonstrates a Dynamic Energy & Process Management Platform to monitor, analyse and optimize the most energy-intensive industrial processes, by managing properly emerging demand response mechanisms and providing plant and process flexibility as well as offering grid services. The unique premise of FLEXIndustries, is the optimal integration of i) innovative energy generation, storage and conversion assets (e.g., BESS and waste heat recovery solutions based on novel HPs, ORC and heat exchangers systems), ii) smart and digital tools for optimised operation and control, all supported by iii) novel business models and market mechanisms for enhanced industrial flexibility. Overall, FLEXIndustries has the potential to save: a) ≥ 159 GWh/ y of Primary Energy in total, b) ≥ 6.0 M€/y Life Cycle Costs on demo scale and c) ≥ 33,111 CO2-eq/y emissions at project level. Demonstration will take place in 6 industrial facilities in 5 reference countries (Turkey, Greece, Poland, Bulgaria, and Italy) and will feature: a) energy efficiency and operational flexibility along with process redesign/modification, b) increased levels of electrification, digitalisation and automation, c) enhanced user satisfaction and grid flexibility services, and d) decreased environmental footprint. A highly competent team of 16 Large Enterprises, 6 Research Institutes, 8 SMEs, 2 Universities and 3 Non-profit Organizations are assembled to ensure FLEXIndustries success

objective_excerpt.en: A sustainable Circular Economy in the wind sector requires to solve the End of Life problematic of the Wind Turbine Blades, prioritizing environmental factors and fairly sharing the efforts to overcome the technologic, economic and social barriers among all the key actors. To this end, EoLO-HUBs will develop 3 open hubs to co-design, co-create and demonstrate new technologies, organizational structures, business models and legal recommendations to implement CE according to the needs of the different European regions. The Knowledge Hub will connect stakeholders to effectively collaborate on similar initiatives, sharing data and spilling over good practices to replicate success stories during and after the project. The other 2 hubs will build a large-scale demonstration covering the full value chain for WTB reusing and recycling from the dismantling to the valorisation in heavy composite sectors through efficient waste recycling solutions, while specific needs of EoL composites in wind technology are representing.  The Onshore Hub will include the necessity of implementing a Zero-pollution and mobile system for dismantling onshore technologies without jeopardise the environment and maximising the recovering of paints and coatings as well as enabling the recyclability of chemical building blocks (solvolysis). The Multi-sectorial and Offshore Hub will include the necessity of adapting current high volume composite recycling technologies (pyrolysis) to obtain a high yield of rGF and cGF in a Zero-waste approach collaborating with other sectors as well as to demonstrate how to prepare the gateways for offshore technologies to connect to the new value chain for recycling WTB. In this way, EoLO-HUBs will create a long-term collaboration of key actors with access to relevant demonstration scenarios to ensure the recycling of almost 90% of the WTB materials, creating a circular economy that generates jobs and reduce greenhouse gas emission by 2030.

objective_excerpt.en: PILATUS is a 3-year project aiming to demonstrate by 2025 three digitalised pilot lines for the production in Europe of silicon wafers, solar cells, and modules. PILATUS will leverage on the patented and already proven back-contacted silicon heterojunction “tunnel-IBC” technology to ensure achieving its ambitious targets. PILATUS will prove a production capacity of 15 MW for M10 silicon wafers in Norway using polysilicon from Europe and demonstrate the feasibility of an expansion to 5 GW wafer production capacity. PILATUS’ PV module pilot line will reach a minimum of 170 MW of annual production capacity, accompanied with 190 MW cell capacity that by itself adds 30% to the current total capacity for PV cell production in Europe. Combining inline metrology and outdoor monitoring with the support of Industry 4.0 concepts all along the production chain, the cells and modules fabricated on PILATUS’ pilot lines will be analysed and feedback provided to the manufacturing process to ensure reaching ≥ 90 % yield at the end of the project. With the goal to establish PV modules with high durability, PILATUS targets to demonstrate the way towards > 40 years product lifetime by gaining fundamental insights into the degradation mechanisms and providing mitigation solutions thanks to the inline and outdoor metrology units that will be developed in the scope of the project. Further, PILATUS will prove a reduced environmental footprint compared to current technologies by demonstrating modules fully made from recycled materials, eco-design practices to facilitate the dismantling of PV panels, and manufacturing plants compliant with environmental standards. In short, PILATUS will contribute to re-building a “made in Europe”, leading-edge, competitive PV industry with the entire value chain been retained in Europe, compliant to the latest environmental standards, hence fostering the affordability, the security of supply, and the sustainability of the future EU low-carbon energy system.

observed.zh: 官方记录Hadean Energy利用氢能示范设施测试千瓦级电解槽组件，并将国际研究合作作为产业任务的一部分。
observed.en: Official material records Hadean Energy testing a kilowatt-class electrolyser bundle and international research cooperation within the mission.

constraints.zh: 出口价值链取决于海外需求、成本与认证；研发合作不能消除这些市场约束。
constraints.en: Export chains depend on external demand, costs and certification; research partnerships do not remove these constraints.

transfer.zh: 用产业任务统筹研究和试验，但将技术验证、市场承诺与规模化投资分别评估。
transfer.en: Coordinate research and testing through a mission, while assessing technical validation, demand commitments and scale-up separately.

title.zh: 联合国气候技术中心与网络需求驱动援助
title.en: CTCN demand-driven technology assistance

aliases: Climate Technology Centre and Network
气候技术中心与网络

summary.zh: 由发展中国家提出技术需求，经国家联络机构确认后，组织专家网络提供适配当地的技术支持。
summary.en: Developing countries request technology assistance through national focal points, with expert networks providing locally tailored support.

actors.zh: CTCN、国家指定实体、申请机构以及实施技术支持的网络成员。
actors.en: CTCN, National Designated Entities, applicants and implementing network members.

mechanism.zh: 国家联络机构核对需求与本国优先事项；中心与申请方形成支持方案，再选择实施伙伴。
mechanism.en: National focal points check alignment with priorities; CTCN and applicants design support plans and select implementing partners.

observed.zh: 官方流程依次包括国家需求确认、共同设计技术支持方案、选择实施伙伴；服务覆盖能力建设、技术试点与制度框架。
observed.en: The documented process covers national needs confirmation, support-plan design and implementing-partner selection, spanning capacity, pilots and institutional frameworks.

constraints.zh: 技术适配依赖受援机构能力和后续实施资源，专家报告不能自动转化为持续运营。
constraints.en: Suitability depends on recipient capabilities and implementation resources; expert advice does not automatically create sustained operation.

transfer.zh: 后发国家可用明确场景提出需求，将外部专家支持与本地组织、人员培训和后续融资衔接。
transfer.en: Latecomer countries can specify application needs and link external expertise with local organisations, training and follow-on financing.

title.zh: 欧洲InnoEnergy教育、创新与创业协同
title.en: European InnoEnergy education–innovation–enterprise model

aliases: EIT InnoEnergy
InnoEnergy

summary.zh: 将创业教育、企业加速与能源创新支持结合，连接高校、产业和金融参与方。
summary.en: Entrepreneurial education, acceleration and energy-innovation support connect higher education, industry and finance.

actors.zh: EIT支持建立的知识与创新共同体、大学、企业、投资者与创新团队。
actors.en: An EIT-established Knowledge and Innovation Community, universities, firms, investors and innovators.

mechanism.zh: 国际教育与创业支持相衔接，通过网络连接业务开发、产业资源和创新技术商业化。
mechanism.en: International education connects with venture support and networks for business development, industrial resources and commercialisation.

observed.zh: EIT资料记载共同体2010年建立，创业加速、国际硕士教育和产业网络被组合为能源技术商业化支持体系。
observed.en: EIT documentation records establishment in 2010 and a combination of acceleration, international master's education and industrial networks supporting commercialisation.

constraints.zh: 平台网络可提供入口，但资本投入和市场准入仍需按技术与国家情境判断，不能由成员关系推定收益。
constraints.en: Networks provide access, but investment and market entry remain technology- and country-specific; membership does not establish returns.

transfer.zh: 将研究生培养与产业问题、创业实践和资本对接结合，保持技术能力与商业验证并重。
transfer.en: Combine graduate education with industrial challenges, venture practice and finance while retaining both technical and market validation.

title.zh: 巴西EMBRAPII产业研发与国际合作
title.en: Brazil EMBRAPII industrial R&D and international cooperation

aliases: EMBRAPII
Embrapii
巴西工业研究与创新

summary.zh: 经认证的研究单元与企业共同定义研发项目，并以公共支持分担前竞争阶段的研发成本。
summary.en: Accredited research units and firms define R&D projects, with public support sharing pre-competitive development costs.

actors.zh: EMBRAPII、巴西研究与技术机构、企业及国际合作资助伙伴。
actors.en: EMBRAPII, Brazilian research and technology institutions, companies and international funding partners.

mechanism.zh: 企业直接与研究单元协商技术和商业范围；国际项目由各国伙伴分别向本国支持机构申报。
mechanism.en: Firms negotiate technical and commercial scope with research units; international partners apply through their respective national agencies.

observed.zh: 国际合作流程要求巴西企业与国外伙伴分别在本国申报，企业可直接与研究单元协商技术与商业范围。
observed.en: International procedures require Brazilian and foreign partners to apply domestically; firms negotiate technical and commercial scope with research units.

constraints.zh: 研究单元能力与企业需求是否匹配，以及两国资助条件是否同步，是跨境项目的重要约束。
constraints.en: The fit between research capabilities and firm demand, alongside coordination of national funding conditions, constrains cross-border projects.

transfer.zh: 后发国家可认证已有研究机构，而非先新建大量机构，以产业合同和绩效要求组织国际研发接口。
transfer.en: Latecomer countries can accredit existing institutions and organise international R&D around industrial contracts and capability requirements.

title.zh: Eurostars中小企业跨境联合研发
title.en: Eurostars SME-led cross-border R&D

aliases: Eurostars
欧洲之星研发

summary.zh: 由创新型中小企业牵头国际研发联合体，以市场导向项目连接不同国家的企业和科研团队。
summary.en: Innovative SMEs lead international consortia linking companies and researchers through market-oriented R&D.

actors.zh: Eureka网络、欧盟及参与国资助机构；瑞士由Innosuisse提供项目支持。
actors.en: Eureka, the EU and participating funding agencies, including Innosuisse in Switzerland.

mechanism.zh: 共同项目与国际评审对接国家资助体系；资格、可资助费用和支持强度受参与方所在地规则约束。
mechanism.en: Joint projects connect international assessment with national funding; eligibility and support remain subject to domestic rules.

observed.zh: 公开资格指南要求创新型中小企业牵头并组成独立实体联合体；瑞士官方页面说明其如何对接国际项目与本国支持。
observed.en: Public eligibility guidance requires an innovative SME lead and independent consortium entities; Swiss guidance explains the international-to-national funding interface.

constraints.zh: 协调难点在于多国资助节奏、联合体责任和成果分配，而非单纯增加合作伙伴数量。
constraints.en: Coordination centres on funding schedules, consortium responsibilities and allocation of results, not partner counts.

transfer.zh: 区域间复制时，应先协调国家资助接口、项目退出与知识产权约定，再开放企业联合申报。
transfer.en: For regional replication, align funding interfaces, exit procedures and IP agreements before opening joint applications.

title.zh: 德国弗劳恩霍夫应用研究与国际合作
title.en: Fraunhofer applied research and international cooperation

aliases: Fraunhofer
弗劳恩霍夫

summary.zh: 以企业委托研发、长期合作和创新集群衔接科学研究与工业应用，并通过国际合作连接外部能力。
summary.en: Contract research, strategic partnerships and innovation clusters connect applied science with industrial use and international capabilities.

actors.zh: 弗劳恩霍夫研究机构、企业、大学及国际合作伙伴。
actors.en: Fraunhofer institutes, companies, universities and international partners.

mechanism.zh: 企业技术需求进入合同研发；长期合作支持连续研发，集群与衍生企业拓展成果转化路径。
mechanism.en: Industrial problems enter contract research; long-term partnerships, clusters and spin-offs provide routes to translation.

observed.zh: 官方合作指南提供合同研发、长期战略伙伴、创新集群和衍生企业四类转化渠道；国际布局结合伙伴与市场分析。
observed.en: Official guidance identifies contract R&D, strategic partnerships, clusters and spin-offs; international engagement includes partner and market assessment.

constraints.zh: 模式依赖稳定的应用研究能力与企业付费需求；研究机构数量并不能替代技术吸收能力。
constraints.en: The model needs sustained applied-research capabilities and firms able to commission research; institute counts cannot substitute for absorptive capacity.

transfer.zh: 先建立面向产业共性难题的研究单元与清晰合同，再开展跨境合作；经费结构需适应当地企业能力。
transfer.en: Build specialised units and clear contracts around industrial problems first; adapt funding arrangements to local firms before scaling international cooperation.

title.zh: 绿色电力未来使命跨国协同
title.en: Green Powered Future Mission collaboration

sector.zh: 电网、储能与可再生能源

aliases: Green Powered Future Mission
绿色电力未来使命

summary.zh: 以共同创新路线图组织高比例可再生电力研究，比较不同地理与气候条件下的系统灵活性和集成路径。
summary.en: A shared roadmap coordinates high-renewable power research across geographies, focusing on flexibility and system integration.

actors.zh: 中国、意大利和英国共同牵头，其他参与方提供研究、政策和示范合作。
actors.en: China, Italy and the UK co-lead, with other participants contributing research, policy and demonstration cooperation.

mechanism.zh: 将技术优先事项、示范项目、数字工具与可复制性研究衔接，形成供不同国家选择的技术路径。
mechanism.en: Innovation priorities connect with demonstrations, digital tools and replicability studies to develop pathways for different countries.

observed.zh: 共同路线图于2021年11月发布，围绕可再生电力、系统灵活性和集成安排研究与示范；中国、意大利、英国共同牵头。
observed.en: A roadmap released in November 2021 organises research and demonstrations on renewable power, flexibility and integration, co-led by China, Italy and the UK.

constraints.zh: 电力市场、气候条件和灵活性资源不同，单一技术组合难以直接复制到所有国家。
constraints.en: Power markets, climate and flexibility resources differ; no single technology mix is directly transferable everywhere.

transfer.zh: 跨国共同任务应比较系统条件，在当地电网约束下验证储能、需求响应和控制技术的组合。
transfer.en: Joint tasks should compare system conditions and validate storage, demand response and control combinations under local grid constraints.

title.zh: 南非HySA氢能研发与产业试验
title.en: South Africa HySA research and industrial testing

aliases: Hydrogen South Africa
HySA Infrastructure
南非HySA

summary.zh: 高校、研究机构和企业围绕氢能设备与燃料电池开展研发，通过本地试验设施连接技术与产业应用。
summary.en: Universities, research institutions and firms develop hydrogen equipment and fuel cells, using local facilities to connect research and industrial applications.

actors.zh: 南非DSTI、西北大学、CSIR等HySA机构；部分示范与丰田南非合作。
actors.en: South Africa DSTI, North-West University and CSIR/HySA institutions; Toyota South Africa participates in a demonstration.

mechanism.zh: 专业中心形成研发分工，试验平台支持原型、部件和系统验证，产业伙伴参与应用示范。
mechanism.en: Specialised centres divide research tasks; platforms support prototype and system validation with industrial demonstrations.

observed.zh: 移动加氢设施于2025年2月建成，DSTI公开其与丰田南非的合作及设施交付；CSIR报告记录HySA专业中心间的分工。
observed.en: A mobile hydrogen refuelling facility was completed in February 2025; DSTI documents Toyota South Africa cooperation and handover, while CSIR records specialised centres.

constraints.zh: 示范设施证明了工程试验能力，但不能单独证明大规模氢能市场成熟或项目盈利。
constraints.en: Demonstration facilities establish testing capabilities, not the maturity or profitability of a large hydrogen market.

transfer.zh: 资源优势需与本地研发、知识产权和工程技能结合；先形成可测试的产品与应用再扩大产业链投资。
transfer.en: Combine resource advantages with local R&D, IP and engineering skills, testing products and applications before expanding investment.

title.zh: 国际数据空间可信数据共享
title.en: International Data Spaces trusted data sharing

aliases: International Data Spaces
国际数据空间

summary.zh: 通过参考架构、连接器与认证规则组织企业间数据共享，强调数据提供者对使用条件的控制。
summary.en: Reference architecture, connectors and certification organise inter-company sharing with provider control over data-use conditions.

actors.zh: 国际数据空间协会、成员组织、连接器开发者与数据空间参与方。
actors.en: IDSA, member organisations, connector developers and data-space participants.

mechanism.zh: 公开技术规范和认证框架连接身份、可信交换和数据使用控制，为协同研发与产业数据利用提供接口。
mechanism.en: Public specifications and certification connect identity, trusted exchange and usage control for research and industrial data collaboration.

observed.zh: 协会公开参考架构和认证框架，采用连接器、数据使用条件和可追溯机制组织可信交换，提供区别于全面集中数据的平台路径。
observed.en: Public architecture and certification frameworks use connectors, usage conditions and traceability for trusted exchange, offering an alternative to fully centralised platforms.

constraints.zh: 该案例为制度与技术基础设施对照，不是能源项目成果；技术可互通和法律可跨境须分别判断。
constraints.en: This is an institutional/technical comparator, not an energy-project outcome; technical interoperability and legal transferability are separate questions.

transfer.zh: 能源数据平台可采用可控共享而非全面集中：先界定数据用途、访问权限和审计责任，再连接多方。
transfer.en: Energy platforms can favour controlled sharing over full centralisation, defining purposes, access and audit responsibilities before interconnection.

title.zh: 国际能源署技术合作计划
title.en: IEA Technology Collaboration Programme

aliases: Technology Collaboration Programme
国际能源署技术合作计划

summary.zh: 通过跨国专家组开展能源技术研发与示范，将政府、研究机构和产业需求连接到共同任务。
summary.en: International expert groups connect governments, research organisations and industry through energy RD&D tasks.

actors.zh: 国际能源署合作框架；各技术合作计划的政府、产业及研究参与方。
actors.en: IEA cooperation framework and the government, industry and research participants of individual programmes.

mechanism.zh: 围绕共同技术问题组织任务，参与方共享专业知识与研究工作；具体任务和资源承诺由各计划安排。
mechanism.en: Participants organise tasks around shared technical problems; individual programmes arrange work and resource commitments.

observed.zh: 框架成立于1975年；官网按技术领域提供在运行的合作计划目录，供研究机构与产业方识别合作入口。
observed.en: Established in 1975, the framework provides a directory of ongoing programmes by technology area for research and industrial participants.

constraints.zh: 共同目标有助于合作持续，但各方投入、数据权限和成果使用仍需在任务层面明确。
constraints.en: Shared goals support cooperation, but task-level agreements still need to define contributions, data access and use of results.

transfer.zh: 后发国家可从有本地应用场景的任务切入，以试验数据和专业人才交换知识，而非复制全部研发体系。
transfer.en: Latecomer countries can enter tasks relevant to local applications, contributing test data and expertise rather than duplicating entire R&D systems.

title.zh: IECRE可再生能源国际合格评定
title.en: IECRE renewable-energy conformity assessment

aliases: IECRE
可再生能源合格评定体系

summary.zh: 以统一规则和国际标准组织可再生能源设备合格评定，推动认证机构与测试实验室之间的一致实施。
summary.en: Common rules and international standards organise renewable-equipment conformity assessment across certification bodies and test laboratories.

actors.zh: IEC及IECRE体系中的认证机构、实验室、供应商和终端用户。
actors.en: IEC and certification bodies, laboratories, suppliers and end users participating in IECRE.

mechanism.zh: 规则统一证书含义、信息提交与合格评定流程，寻求减少重复工作并协调体系内分歧。
mechanism.en: Rules align certificate meanings, information requirements and assessment procedures, seeking to reduce duplication and resolve disagreements.

observed.zh: 体系规则统一证书含义和信息要求，公开证书平台支持检索已签发记录，为设备供应链提供可核查的合格评定入口。
observed.en: System rules align certificate meanings and information requirements; a public registry enables checks of issued certificates for equipment supply chains.

constraints.zh: 标准、检测能力与市场监管要求需要共同衔接，国际证书不能替代目的地法律合规。
constraints.en: Standards, testing capabilities and market rules need alignment; international certificates do not replace destination-law compliance.

transfer.zh: 对出口导向产业，建设可参与国际合格评定的实验室，比只增加本地标准数量更有针对性。
transfer.en: For export industries, develop laboratories able to participate in international assessment rather than merely adding domestic standards.

title.zh: 摩洛哥Green Innoboost绿色创新支持
title.en: Morocco Green Innoboost green innovation support

aliases: Green Innoboost
绿色Innoboost

summary.zh: 将创新资金、创业支持与绿色能源试验设施结合，帮助技术团队连接科研平台和商业伙伴。
summary.en: Innovation finance, venture support and green-energy test facilities connect technology teams with research platforms and commercial partners.

actors.zh: IRESEN、创新团队、大学、企业及潜在投资者。
actors.en: IRESEN, innovators, universities, companies and prospective investors.

mechanism.zh: 提供Green Energy Park等设施入口，同时支持采购服务、技术试验与投资者联系。
mechanism.en: Access to facilities such as Green Energy Park is combined with services procurement, testing and investor connections.

observed.zh: 国际能源署记录资金、设施和投资者对接支持，并指出IRESEN支持科特迪瓦太阳能研究平台，以测试热带条件下的技术。
observed.en: IEA documents finance, facilities and investor connections, and records IRESEN support for a solar research platform in Côte d'Ivoire to test tropical conditions.

constraints.zh: 设施可用性必须与工程辅导和本地市场需求结合；试验条件不同会影响技术适配。
constraints.en: Facility access must be combined with engineering support and local demand; environmental differences affect suitability.

transfer.zh: 将公共试验平台与创业服务打包，跨区域推广时先验证当地气候、维护能力和付费需求。
transfer.en: Bundle public testing with venture services, and validate climate, maintenance capabilities and customer demand before regional transfer.

title.zh: 国际太阳能联盟STAR-C能力建设网络
title.en: ISA STAR-C capacity-building network

aliases: STAR-C
STAR Centre
Solar Technology Application Resource
太阳能技术应用资源中心

summary.zh: 建设太阳能技术与应用资源中心网络，把培训、共享设施、测试和技术应用能力带入成员国。
summary.en: Solar technology resource centres connect training, shared facilities, testing and application capabilities across member countries.

actors.zh: 国际太阳能联盟、成员国与当地培训及技术机构；联盟由印度和法国共同发起。
actors.en: ISA, member countries and local training/technical institutions; the alliance originated with India and France.

mechanism.zh: 以国家或区域中心承接技能培养、技术知识和应用服务，连接本地机构与国际太阳能能力网络。
mechanism.en: National or regional centres provide skills, knowledge and application services, linking local institutions with an international network.

observed.zh: 官方项目资料列明资源中心的培训、测试、孵化及标准化功能，并记录2018—2019年来自25国的133人参加培训。
observed.en: Official project material identifies training, testing, incubation and standardisation functions and records 133 trainees from 25 countries in 2018–2019.

constraints.zh: 设备部署之外，本地运维人员、机构能力和可持续服务经费决定中心是否有效。
constraints.en: Beyond equipment, local maintenance skills, institutional capacity and sustainable service funding determine usefulness.

transfer.zh: 通过已有高校或技术机构构建区域资源中心，把人才培养与项目运维需求一起安排。
transfer.en: Build centres through existing universities or technical institutions and connect training with project operation needs.

title.zh: ITER国际聚变研发与实物贡献机制
title.en: ITER international fusion research and in-kind contributions

aliases: ITER Organization
ITER project
国际热核聚变实验堆

summary.zh: 成员共同建设大型聚变科研装置，通过实物贡献、共享实验结果和知识产权安排组织跨国研发。
summary.en: Members jointly develop a fusion research facility through in-kind contributions and arrangements for shared results and intellectual property.

actors.zh: 中国、欧盟、印度、日本、韩国、俄罗斯、美国；装置位于法国。
actors.en: China, EU, India, Japan, Korea, Russia and the US; the facility is located in France.

mechanism.zh: 成员分担建设等成本，国内机构对接设备供给，国际协议界定组织治理及成果共享。
mechanism.en: Members share costs and supply equipment through domestic agencies; international agreements define governance and sharing of results.

observed.zh: 成员共同承担建设、运行和退役成本，并共享实验结果与项目产生的知识产权；装置用于验证聚变的科学和技术可行性。
observed.en: Members share construction, operation and decommissioning costs, experimental results and generated IP; the facility tests scientific and technological feasibility of fusion.

constraints.zh: 大型设施合作要求长期资金承诺、接口标准与可执行的治理安排，不能等同于一般企业研发联盟。
constraints.en: Large-facility cooperation requires long-term financing, interface standards and implementable governance, unlike a routine business R&D alliance.

transfer.zh: 对高投入共性技术，可学习共享设施与贡献责任设计；应限定任务边界并明确成果使用和退出条件。
transfer.en: For capital-intensive technologies, shared facilities and contribution responsibilities are transferable, provided task boundaries and result-use conditions are explicit.

title.zh: 肯尼亚气候创新中心本地创业与国际连接
title.en: Kenya Climate Innovation Center local ventures and global links

sector.zh: 太阳能、电动出行与气候技术
sector.en: Solar, electric mobility and climate technology

aliases: Kenya Climate Innovation Center
肯尼亚气候创新中心

summary.zh: 向本地气候企业提供技术和商业支持，并通过大学及国际伙伴合作连接创新竞赛、孵化和融资。
summary.en: Local climate ventures receive technical and business support, linked to competitions, incubation and finance through university and international partnerships.

actors.zh: KCIC、肯尼亚企业、斯特拉斯莫尔大学，以及瑞士驻肯尼亚使馆和SICPA等合作方。
actors.en: KCIC, Kenyan ventures, Strathmore University, the Swiss Embassy in Kenya and SICPA.

mechanism.zh: 以创业团队的实际环境问题为起点，连接技术支持、市场信息、设施与融资准备。
mechanism.en: Support starts from practical environmental problems and links expertise, market intelligence, facilities and finance readiness.

observed.zh: 中心自2012年开展企业支持，公开太阳能、电动出行等领域服务；清洁技术竞赛与大学、瑞士机构合作吸纳早期团队。
observed.en: Operating since 2012, the centre documents solar and electric-mobility support; a university and Swiss-partner competition engages early-stage teams.

constraints.zh: 此模式侧重技术吸收和创业能力，并非所有团队都承担基础科学研究；竞赛入选不证明商业成功。
constraints.en: The focus is absorption and entrepreneurship rather than basic research in every venture; selection is not commercial success.

transfer.zh: 能力有限地区可先补足技术、市场与融资之间的接口，以应用需求筛选创新，而非照搬大型研发中心。
transfer.en: Regions with limited capacity can strengthen technical, market and finance interfaces, selecting demand-led innovations rather than copying large research centres.

title.zh: 麻省理工能源计划产业会员合作
title.en: MIT Energy Initiative industry membership

aliases: MIT Energy Initiative
麻省理工能源计划

summary.zh: 产业会员将现实能源问题与MIT研究团队连接，通过研究支持和行业交流对接科研议题。
summary.en: Industry membership connects real-world energy problems with MIT research teams through research support and exchange.

actors.zh: MIT Energy Initiative、不同规模企业以及公共部门会员。
actors.en: MIT Energy Initiative, companies of different sizes and public-sector members.

mechanism.zh: 会员提供产业问题与研究机会，研究团队开展相关研究；分层参与方式拓展合作入口。
mechanism.en: Members bring industrial problems and research opportunities; tiered participation provides different entry routes.

observed.zh: 会员制度面向不同规模的企业及公共部门，提供研究交流、合作机会和跨学科能源研究的参与渠道。
observed.en: Membership offers research exchange, collaboration opportunities and interdisciplinary energy engagement to firms of different sizes and public-sector organisations.

constraints.zh: 大企业与中小企业的研究预算和议题影响力可能不同，应单独安排可负担的参与方式。
constraints.en: Large and smaller firms differ in research budgets and agenda-setting capacity; affordable participation routes matter.

transfer.zh: 高校平台可将产业问题清单、跨学科研发和可分层参与的合作制度结合，避免只依赖单一资助方。
transfer.en: University platforms can combine industrial problem lists, interdisciplinary research and tiered engagement to avoid dependence on one sponsor.

title.zh: 英国ORE Catapult风电开放测试
title.en: UK ORE Catapult open wind testing

aliases: ORE Catapult
Offshore Renewable Energy Catapult

summary.zh: 开放大型测试设施与工程能力，联合产业伙伴验证风机、叶片和电气系统，衔接研发与认证需求。
summary.en: Large-scale facilities and engineering expertise help industrial partners validate turbines, blades and electrical systems for development and certification.

actors.zh: ORE Catapult、GE Renewable Energy等产业伙伴，以及研究与认证相关参与方。
actors.en: ORE Catapult, industrial partners including GE Renewable Energy, and research/certification participants.

mechanism.zh: 采用代表性试验与电网模拟等能力，减少研发测试对现场条件的依赖，连接研究、工程与产品验证。
mechanism.en: Representative testing and grid emulation connect research and engineering with product validation, reducing reliance on field conditions.

observed.zh: 公开资料记录GE风机测试合作；评估报告说明eGrid验证结果被英国电网接受用于替代部分现场数据。
observed.en: Public records document GE turbine testing; an evaluation describes National Grid acceptance of eGrid results in place of field data.

constraints.zh: 测试可支持合格评定，但不等于所有目的地市场自动认可；设备尺度和利用率影响设施经济性。
constraints.en: Testing can support conformity assessment but does not guarantee acceptance in every market; scale and utilisation affect facility economics.

transfer.zh: 共享大型测试设施比企业各自建设更适合共性验证需求，但需同步设计认可范围和产业参与机制。
transfer.en: Shared facilities suit common validation needs, provided recognition scope and industrial participation are designed together.

title.zh: IEA PVPS光伏可靠性跨气候研究
title.en: IEA PVPS Task 13 cross-climate reliability research

aliases: IEA PVPS Task 13
IEA-PVPS Task 13
PVPS Task 13
光伏可靠性任务13

summary.zh: 汇集不同气候区光伏运行资料与试验经验，支持组件质量、可靠性和发电量评估。
summary.en: Operating data and testing experience from different climates support assessments of PV quality, reliability and yield.

actors.zh: IEA PVPS Task 13研究团队及参与机构、行业使用者。
actors.en: IEA PVPS Task 13 researchers, participating institutions and industry users.

mechanism.zh: 跨区域研究对比新应用和环境条件，形成可供项目开发、运营与质量管理使用的报告。
mechanism.en: Cross-regional research compares applications and environments, producing reports for development, operation and quality management.

observed.zh: 官方列明2026—2029年跨气候光伏研究，2026年项目决策报告把质量管理、发电性能和经济价值连贯分析。
observed.en: Official material identifies the 2026–2029 cross-climate research phase; a 2026 report links quality management, performance and economic value.

constraints.zh: 运行数据的可比性取决于试验条件、采样和指标口径；建议并非具有强制力的全球统一标准。
constraints.en: Comparability depends on testing conditions, sampling and indicator conventions; guidance is not a binding global standard.

transfer.zh: 技术引进应配套本地气候运行数据与可靠性验证，利用国际研究降低重复试验而非省略当地验证。
transfer.en: Technology adoption should include local operating data and reliability checks, using international work to reduce duplication rather than eliminate local validation.

title.zh: 印美太阳能研究联合体SERIIUS
title.en: India–US Solar Energy Research Institute SERIIUS

aliases: SERIIUS
Solar Energy Research Institute for India

summary.zh: 联合印度与美国研究力量，围绕光伏和光热发电技术成本开展协作，衔接两国太阳能发展需求。
summary.en: Indian and US researchers collaborated on PV and concentrating solar power costs, aligning research with both countries' solar needs.

actors.zh: 印度科学研究院、NREL、桑迪亚国家实验室及相关研发伙伴。
actors.en: Indian Institute of Science, NREL, Sandia National Laboratories and research partners.

mechanism.zh: 联合体以共同技术任务组织研究；光热研究包括发电循环、集热器和接收器等环节。
mechanism.en: Shared tasks organise research, including power cycles, collectors and receivers for concentrating solar power.

observed.zh: 桑迪亚2012年报告记录光伏、光热研究任务；其公开的2016年光热循环技术经济论文注明SERIIUS资助，形成可追溯科研成果。
observed.en: Sandia's 2012 report records PV and CSP tasks; a public 2016 solar-cycle technoeconomic paper acknowledges SERIIUS support, providing a traceable research output.

constraints.zh: 这是历史合作案例，不能由早期研究计划推定目前仍按原规模运行，也不能把性能目标当成已实现指标。
constraints.en: This is a historical case: early plans do not establish current scale or achieved performance.

transfer.zh: 适合比较具有相近技术需求但不同应用条件的国家，联合任务需包含面向当地条件的试验和人才培养。
transfer.en: Joint tasks are useful where technical needs overlap but application conditions differ; local testing and training should be included.

title.zh: WIPO GREEN绿色技术供需对接
title.en: WIPO GREEN technology matchmaking

sector.zh: 绿色技术与知识产权交易

aliases: WIPO GREEN
世界知识产权组织绿色

summary.zh: 通过技术与需求数据库连接绿色技术供给者和寻求解决方案的机构，提供许可、合作和合资线索。
summary.en: A technology-and-needs database connects green-technology suppliers and seekers, providing leads for licensing, collaboration and joint ventures.

actors.zh: 世界知识产权组织、技术持有者、企业、机构和非政府组织。
actors.en: WIPO, technology holders, companies, institutions and NGOs.

mechanism.zh: 供给方发布技术，需求方描述应用问题，平台开展自动匹配并连接技术与潜在使用者。
mechanism.en: Suppliers list technologies and seekers state application needs; automated matching connects potential counterparts.

observed.zh: 公开数据库覆盖从原型到可销售产品，允许发布出售、许可、合作和合资信息，并支持技术与需求的自动匹配。
observed.en: The public database covers prototypes through marketable products, with sale, licence, collaboration and joint-venture information and automated matching.

constraints.zh: 许可条件、适用场景与技术成熟度仍须交易双方协商，平台无法替代知识产权尽调。
constraints.en: Licensing terms, use conditions and maturity still require negotiation; the platform cannot replace IP due diligence.

transfer.zh: 开放平台宜同时结构化记录技术能力和真实需求，补充许可状态、试验条件和联络渠道。
transfer.en: Open platforms should structure both capabilities and demand, with licensing status, test conditions and contact routes.

title.zh: 熔融浸渗固态陶瓷电解质
title.en: Melt-Infiltration Solid Electrolyte

aliases: Melt-Infiltration Solid Electrolyte
熔融浸渗固态陶瓷电解质

summary.zh: Sila团队拟开发高能量密度固态陶瓷锂电池，针对传统陶瓷电解质和隔膜厚重、制造难的问题研究新型电解质构建工艺，以减小非活性材料体积。
summary.en: Sila Nanotechnologies will develop solid-state ceramic lithium batteries with high energy density. Traditional methods using ceramic electrolytes significantly reduces a battery's volumetric energy density because the materials are relatively bulky. Commercially produced separator membranes are also expensive and thick because of challenges in fabrication and handling of thinner, defect-free solid-state electrolyte membranes. In addition, such membranes are often air sensitive, have low ionic conductivity, and are susceptible to the growth of branchlike metal fibers called dendrites.…

actors.zh: Sila Nanotechnologies；合作单位：Georgia Institute of Technology、U.S. Army Research Laboratory。
actors.en: Sila Nanotechnologies; named partners: Georgia Institute of Technology; U.S. Army Research Laboratory

mechanism.zh: 电池材料企业、佐治亚理工和陆军研究实验室共同开发固态电解质。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E IONICS research collaboration led by Sila Nanotechnologies with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 2709，IONICS计划。登记资助1,000,000美元；项目期2016-12-01至2018-05-31；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 2709, IONICS. Listed award: USD 1,000,000. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

title.zh: 锂电池高容量纳米结构负极
title.en: Double Energy Density Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

aliases: Double Energy Density Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
锂电池高容量纳米结构负极

summary.zh: Sila与佐治亚理工研究组织拟开发高通量、可放大的纳米结构材料合成方法，在提高锂离子电池负极容量的同时控制充放电体积变化。
summary.en: Sila Nanotechnologies is developing a high-throughput technology for scalable synthesis of high-capacity nanostructured materials for Li-Ion EV batteries. The successful implementation of this technology will allow improvements in energy storage capacity of today's best batteries at half the cost. In contrast to other high-capacity material synthesis technologies, Sila's materials show minimal volume changes during the battery operation, which is a key challenge of next-generation battery anode materials. In addition, Sila's technology may allow for the dramatic enhancements of the batteries'…

actors.zh: Sila Nanotechnologies；合作单位：Georgia Tech Research Corporation。
actors.en: Sila Nanotechnologies; named partners: Georgia Tech Research Corporation

mechanism.zh: 电池材料企业与高校研发组织合作，将高容量材料合成推进至规模化工艺。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E BEEST research collaboration led by Sila Nanotechnologies with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 2800，BEEST计划。登记资助3,225,000美元；项目期2012-10-01至2016-03-31；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 2800, BEEST. Listed award: USD 3,225,000. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

title.zh: SMART-FBS：反应物与膜协同液流电池
title.en: Smart-FBS

aliases: Smart-FBS
SMART-FBS：反应物与膜协同液流电池

summary.zh: 联合技术研究中心团队拟同时开发下一代反应物与低成本高选择性膜，围绕两者相容性设计液流电池，降低体系中主要成本构成。
summary.en: United Technologies Research Center (UTRC) will develop a redox flow battery system that combines next-generation reactants with an inexpensive and highly selective membrane. This SMART-FBS project addresses the two highest cost components in redox flow battery systems: reactants and membranes. The team plans to develop these two components simultaneously using core materials that will work in tandem. Polymer membranes will be developed that include benzimidazole or pyridine structures; ionic conductivity will come from the membrane's structure that allows acid to be imbibed into the polymer.…

actors.zh: United Technologies Research Center (UTRC)；合作单位：Harvard University、University of South Carolina、Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory、Advent Technologies, Inc.。
actors.en: United Technologies Research Center (UTRC); named partners: Harvard University; University of South Carolina; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; Advent Technologies, Inc.

mechanism.zh: 工业研发机构联合高校、实验室及Advent，协同选择活性物质与聚合物膜。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E IONICS research collaboration led by United Technologies Research Center (UTRC) with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 2806，IONICS计划。登记资助3,111,261美元；项目期2017-02-17至2019-11-16；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 2806, IONICS. Listed award: USD 3,111,261. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

title.zh: 液流电池阴离子通道膜
title.en: Anion Channel Membranes

aliases: Anion Channel Membranes
液流电池阴离子通道膜

summary.zh: 科罗拉多大学博尔德团队拟利用纳米孔溶致液晶结构开发氯离子传导膜，结合分子尺寸与电荷排斥抑制阳离子交叉，改善液流电池隔膜性能。
summary.en: The University of Colorado, Boulder (CU-Boulder) will develop a new type of anion-exchange membrane for chloride (Cl-) transport that is based on a nanoporous lyotropic liquid crystal structure that minimizes cation crossover by molecular size-exclusion and charge exclusion. Due to a lack of suitable Cl- conducting membranes, flow batteries often use microporous membranes or cation-exchange membranes (CEM) to separate the two electrode chambers. Microporous membranes are inexpensive, but do not provide perfect barriers to intermixing of the reactants (or "crossover") that reduces the…

actors.zh: University of Colorado, Boulder (CU-Boulder)；合作单位：University of California, San Diego、Energy Storage Systems, Inc.。
actors.en: University of Colorado, Boulder (CU-Boulder); named partners: University of California, San Diego; Energy Storage Systems, Inc.

mechanism.zh: 高校膜材料研究与Energy Storage Systems企业应用合作，围绕离子选择性开发隔膜。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E IONICS research collaboration led by University of Colorado, Boulder (CU-Boulder) with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 2808，IONICS计划。登记资助2,508,337美元；项目期2016-12-01至2019-06-30；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 2808, IONICS. Listed award: USD 2,508,337. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

title.zh: 无需水合的质子选择性膜
title.en: Novel Proton-Selective Membranes For Energy Storage

aliases: Novel Proton-Selective Membranes For Energy Storage
无需水合的质子选择性膜

summary.zh: 橡树岭团队拟开发低温且无需水合即可传导质子的膜，面向液流电池、燃料电池与电解槽储能，探索突破传统膜材料含水运行约束的方法。
summary.en: The team led by Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) will design proton-selective membranes for use in storage technologies, such as flow batteries, fuel cells, or electrolyzers for liquid-fuel storage. Current proton-selective membranes (e.g. Nafion) require hydration, but the proposed materials would be the first low-temperature membranes that conduct protons without the need for hydration. The enabling technology relies on making single-layer membranes from graphene or similar materials and supporting them for mechanical stability. The team estimates that these membranes can be…

actors.zh: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL)；合作单位：ITN Energy Systems, Inc.、General Graphene Corporation、New Mexico State University。
actors.en: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL); named partners: ITN Energy Systems, Inc.; General Graphene Corporation; New Mexico State University

mechanism.zh: 国家实验室与ITN、General Graphene及高校联合，将新型质子膜用于电化学系统。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E OPEN 2015 research collaboration led by Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 2854，OPEN 2015计划。登记资助2,776,028美元；项目期2016-05-01至2020-09-30；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 2854, OPEN 2015. Listed award: USD 2,776,028. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

title.zh: 低成本硫锰活性材料液流电池
title.en: High-Performance Flow Battery with Inexpensive Inorganic Reactants

aliases: High-Performance Flow Battery with Inexpensive Inorganic Reactants
低成本硫锰活性材料液流电池

summary.zh: 联合技术研究中心团队拟用丰富、廉价的硫基和锰基活性材料建立液流电池体系，重点解决系统控制与活性物质穿膜交叉问题，面向长时放电需求。
summary.en: The United Technologies Research Center team will develop an energy storage system based on a new flow battery chemistry using inexpensive and readily available sulfur and manganese based active materials. The team will employ innovative strategies to overcome challenges of system control and unwanted crossover of active materials through the membrane. The affordable reactants, paired with the unique requirements for long-duration electricity discharge, present the opportunity for very low cost energy…

actors.zh: United Technologies Research Center (UTRC)；合作单位：University of Colorado, Boulder、Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory、Massachusetts Institute of Technology、Pennsylvania State University。
actors.en: United Technologies Research Center (UTRC); named partners: University of Colorado, Boulder; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Pennsylvania State University

mechanism.zh: 工业研发机构联合多所高校与伯克利实验室，共同开发液流电池化学体系和控制策略。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E DAYS research collaboration led by United Technologies Research Center (UTRC) with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 2888，DAYS计划。登记资助3,798,771美元；项目期2019-01-23至2022-05-31；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 2888, DAYS. Listed award: USD 3,798,771. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

title.zh: 无锂无过渡金属快速充电电池
title.en: Lithium- and Transition Metal-Free High-Energy Fast-Charging Batteries

aliases: Lithium- and Transition Metal-Free High-Energy Fast-Charging Batteries
无锂无过渡金属快速充电电池

summary.zh: 休斯敦大学团队拟以丰富的镁替代锂负极，以炼油或生物炼制获得的有机材料替代传统过渡金属正极，研发兼顾能量与功率密度的快速充电电池。
summary.en: The University of Houston will develop a battery that will match the energy and power densities of lithium-based batteries while excluding lithium, nickel, and cobalt. The proposed battery will substitute lithium-based anodes with energy-dense and abundant magnesium, of which the U.S. has virtually unlimited reserves. Organic materials obtained from oil refineries and biorefineries will replace conventional cathodes based on transition metals, thereby eliminating any requirement for nickel or cobalt. The team's recent technology breakthroughs have overcome the energy and power bottlenecks…

actors.zh: University of Houston；合作单位：LiBeyond LLC、Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America、Twelfth Vertex。
actors.en: University of Houston; named partners: LiBeyond LLC; Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America; Twelfth Vertex

mechanism.zh: 高校联合LiBeyond及丰田北美等工业伙伴，协同开发镁与有机电极体系。
mechanism.en: ARPA-E OPEN 2021 research collaboration led by University of Houston with the named partners.

observed.zh: ARPA-E项目 3004，OPEN 2021计划。登记资助3,400,000美元；项目期2022-06-27至2025-06-26；官网状态为历史项目。
observed.en: ARPA-E project 3004, OPEN 2021. Listed award: USD 3,400,000. Technical objectives are not achieved performance or commercial output.

participants.name: Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America

title.zh: 电动汽车电池管理与控制软件
title.en: Battery Management and Control Software

aliases: Battery Management and Control Software
电动汽车电池管理与控制软件

objective_excerpt.en: MATISSE responds to the fourth bullet of the HORIZON-CL5-2021-D5-01-05 topic “expected outcome”, delivering improved aircraft technologies in the area of multifunctional structures capable of storing electrical energy for hybrid electric aircraft applications. This consists in integrating Li-ion cells into aeronautical composite structures, sharing the load-bearing function with the structure and achieving an aircraft structural element capable of functioning as a battery module. To do so, MATISSE will:• advance Li-ion battery cell technology, in a non-conventional formulation suitable for bearing structural loads: NMC811 (cathode), Si/C (anode) and bicontinuous polymer-ionic quasi-solid-state electrolyte (BCE), i.e. NMC811|BCE|Si/C, achieving 170-270 Wh/kg at cell level;• enable the functional integration of Li-ion cells into solid laminate and sandwich composite structures;• make the structural battery smart, by equipping it with on-cell and in-structure sensors, connected to a chip-based CMU (Cell Monitoring Unit) and PLC (Power Line Communication).MATISSE delivers a multifunctional structure demonstrator capable of power delivery, power management and safety monitoring. This consists of a full-scale wing tip (1.42 m × 0.69 m) for use in place of the current wingtip assembly installed on Pipistrel Velis Electro, embedding a module of 40 battery cells at 72 VDC. This will undergo a comprehensive testing and characterisation campaign, qualifying the technology at TRL 4 at the end of the project (2025). MATISSE will also encompass aspects related to flight certification, life-cycle sustainability and virtual scale-up, paving the way towards the application of structural batteries as an improved performance key enabling technology for next generation commuter and regional hybrid electric aircraft applications.

objective_excerpt.en: As a significant source of greenhouse gasses (GHGs), it is essential that the maritime transport sector focuses on ways to become climate neutral. Partial electrification of power systems has already been adopted as a GHG reduction measure. However, further advances are necessary on such aspects as the provision of high charging powers to minimise costs and improve standardisation. In this context, HYPOBATT will be focused on the development of an interoperable charging solution with a cost-competitive performance.HYPOBATT will deliver a modular, fast, and easy multi-MW recharging system demonstrated in two European ports with fast turnaround times. The project will assess the end-to-end services between both ports, and compatibility with other ports. A modular approach on electrical and mechanical integration will minimize the required connection time, the charging time, land from port side and the number of components and costs. The charging system will be designed to achieve interoperability and compatibility with different electric ships, grid constraints, components, modularity, logistic and handling, monitoring and safety systems, power flow, maintenance, digitalization/automation, cybersecurity, and human element aspects. The standardization of the charging modules, the interfaces, and the communication protocol, will scale up the charger based on and on/offshore sides; flexibility of power levels will be addressed and the impacts on the electrical grid infrastructure and on the battery degradation during fast charging will be minimized.  HYPOBATT unites key actors from the European maritime sector to develop and demonstrate the charging system. A key element is to develop business mechanisms to exploit the flexibility of the charging system amongst shipbuilders, integrators, ports and stakeholders. This will enable the wide adoption of the solution, thus increasing Europe’s lead in fast charging systems.

objective_excerpt.en: The cobalt (Co) and nickel (Ni) demand is expected to be about 20 times higher in 2040 than in 2020. Given that Europe plays only a minor role in the global Ni/Co supply chains, which are concentrated in the DRC, Indonesia and China, we face a serious problem in securing a reliable, affordable and sustainable supply of battery-grade Ni/Co, vital for Europe’s aims to be climate-neutral by 2050. In view of a “domestic and foreign sourcing” procurement model, ENICON exploits the potential of (low-grade) Ni/Co resources within Europe – i.e. sulphidic Ni/Co ores and derived Ni/Co-bearing pyrite and silicate tailings, and limonitic/saprolitic laterite Ni(/Co) ores – while improving and developing the Ni/Co-refining capacity that can process imported ores, concentrates and intermediates. ENICON comprises both major improvements to existing Ni/Co metallurgical unit operations in Europe as well as the development of a new HCl-based route for both Ni/Co sulphide concentrates and laterites. ENICON’s HCl-route dispenses with the old-school hydro-approach of continuously precipitating and redissolving metals that requires lots of chemicals and creates problematic waste streams. The HCl-based route can be extended to the downstream processing of FeNi (Class-II Ni) obtained from laterites; (2) Mixed (Ni/Co) Sulphide/Hydroxide Precipitate (MSP/MHP) from the bioleaching of Co-rich pyrite tailings; and Ni/Co-containing silicate tailings. ENICON targets a “forensic geometallurgy” protocol, making it possible to identify and mitigate the mineralogical and textural reasons for processing losses along existing and new flowsheets. To make the transition to (near) zero-waste processing and to further reduce CO2-footprints, ENICON develops enhanced mineral-matrix valorisation processes. The outputs from ENICON’s group of European Ni/Co mining, processing and refining companies will all be benchmarked in terms of positive environmental and techno-economic impacts against current methods.

objective_excerpt.en: One of the main keys – and possibly THE main key - for a climate neutral Europe are technologies for the storage of renewable energies over longer time at an attractive cost and with an acceptable environmental impact. Renewable electricity and heat can be produced cheaply today and short-term storage solutions for evening out mismatches between production and demand are available at low cost. However, technologies for storing renewables for longer time-spans of months or seasons are scarce and costly and thus not widely used yet. Therefore, the REVEAL project develops a game-changing and unique solution to this challenge, using the conversion of aluminium oxide into aluminium metal (Power-to-Al) in an environmentally friendly way to store renewable energy and produce a ""renewable fuel"" in the form of aluminium. This ground-breaking technical solution will enable to store large amounts of energy with an unmatched energy storage density of over 15 MWh/m3 at an attractively low cost, without losses and with lower environmental impact than today's solutions. For example: cost for converting electricity into a seasonally storable form will be less than 7 ct/kWh, and the easy transportable energy vector can be used for heat and electricity or hydrogen production wherever and whenever needed, in scalable units from few kW to the MW range. Thus, this breakthrough high-density storage solution will enable to cover energy demands flexibly also in small units and off-grid situations, and – above all – in seasons where the demand is much higher than local renewable production could possibly cover. Therefore, with the emerging technology of carbon free reduction of aluminium oxide to aluminium in combination with the release of energy from an aluminium storage vector this project will provide one of the missing pieces of the puzzle for a climate neutral Europe.""

observed.en: Registered technical objectives: Sustainable manufacturing and optimized materials and interfaces for lithium metal batteries with digital quality control

objective_excerpt.en: The SOLiD project will create a sustainable and cost-efficient pilot scale manufacturing process for a high energy density, safe and easily recyclable solid-state Li-metal battery. We will use roll-to-roll (R2R) dry extrusion coating for the blend of cathode active material, solid polymer electrolyte, and conducting additives. R2R slot die coated primers on the cathode current collector will enhance adhesion, performance and corrosion resistance of the cell. The polymer electrolyte layer will be R2R coated, using an optimal design for the slot die head. For the Li metal anode, we will utilize cost-efficient R2R pulsed laser deposition, which enables minimizing the Li thickness down to 5 µm. The Li metal production will be combined with an inline process for interfacial engineering to ensure compatibility with the other layers and stability. The process development will be supported by digitalization methods to go towards zero-defect and cost-efficient manufacturing.The proposed methods enable sustainable manufacturing of Gen. 4b solid state batteries with minimised amount of critical raw materials (Co and Li), and with superior performance and safety: The protective layers enable the use of NMC811, which reduces the amount of Co into minimum without compromising the lifetime, and PLD process helps to minimize the Li thickness. Dry coating eliminates the use of toxic solvents and energy-consuming drying steps, and the digital quality control will reduce the amount of waste. The thickness of each layer will be minimized to reach energy density above 900 Wh/l. Cost will be reduced by cost-effective production methods and by maximizing the yield. Safety and long cycle life are  guaranteed by the solid electrolyte and the protective interlayers. Supported by the life-cycle thinking and stakeholder engagement, the SOLiD project will enable the design for a sustainable solid state battery factory of the future.

objective_excerpt.en: FRESH aims to contribute to reducing the European Union’s dependence on fossil fuels for power generation, providing a cushion for the intermittent character of renewable electricity generation leading to stable, more predictable prices for renewable electricity, which is crucial for the future development of large-scale renewable power generation, and therefore, the energy transition. The project will achieve this through the development, construction and validation at TRL 4, of an integrated, cost competitive process for conversion of CO2 to potassium formate using an electrocatalytic process powered by renewable electricity. The highly stable potassium formate generated by the reactor will be stored safely for long periods (from short term or seasonal) in tanks. The subsequent conversion of the stored potassium formate to electricity on demand will use a direct fuel cell system. The project includes development of the individual components (CO2 to formate and formate to electricity), CO2 sourcing and purification and ultimately the construction and validation of an integrated protoype at TRL 4. This will be achieved by the implementation of a series of interconnected work packages. FRESH is structured around five technical work packages (WPs 2-6) and two ‘enabling/value adding’ work packages (WPs 1 and 7), supporting dissemination, exploitation and management activities. FRESH addresses the work program topic by (1) developing a new renewable energy storage technology (2) highly workable concept & approach, (3) implementation work plan & strategy, (4) a validated prototype at TRL 4, (5) participants with excellent track records for project execution and exploitation  and (6) comprehensive LCA and TEA and energy market evaluation of this new technology. The consortium consists of 7 partners of which 1 research institute (ICCOM), 4 industrial partners (COVAL, ENGIE laboelec, HYSYTECH, eRisk) and 2 universities (FZJ and DTU) from 5 EU member states.

objective_excerpt.en: LiCORNE aims to establish the first-ever Li supply chain in Europe. The goal is to increase the European Li processing and refining capacity for producing battery-grade chemicals from ores, brines, tailings and off-specification battery cathode materials. This supply chain encompasses five large primary resource owners (including one of the world leader in Li production) having resources of ~7.8 Mt lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE), in which 2.7 Mt LCE are located in Europe. The European primary resources that are considered in LiCORNE would be enough to supply ~3000 GWh of batteries (i.e., ~10 years to the expected 300 GWh/year production capacity in Europe by 2030). Additionally, the value chain includes a cathode manufacturer who will be able to reuse valuable Li, Co and Ni that will be recycled from waste cathode material, and one producer and distributor of battery-grade Li-chemicals. LiCORNE will investigate 14 different groundbreaking technologies that have been selected for their potential to operate at low CAPEX and OPEX, low carbon footprint, flexibility and industrial scalability. Those technologies are led by 8 top R&D centers in Europe to tackle the main bottlenecks in Li processing and recovery. During 2.5 years, R&D partners will investigate those technologies and bring their TRL from 2 to 4. After this phase, and guided by LCA and LCCA, the most promising technologies will be selected for upscaling to TRL5. During this phase a prototype system will be constructed and demonstrated at TRL5 to produce ~1 kg of battery-grade Li-chemicals (i.e., LiOH∙H2O, Li2CO3 or Li-metal) from ores, brines, tailings and waste cathode material, with the recycling of Co and Ni from the latter. Results will be communicated and disseminated to a wide range of stakeholders and a first business model for a full and optimized Li supply chain in Europe will be established based on the results of the project and cost of Li produced.

Halide solid state batteries for ELectric vEhicles aNd Aircrafts  (HELENA) responds to the need of the development of a safe, novel high energy efficiency and power density solid state battery (4b generation batteries) cells, based on high capacity Ni-rich cathode (NMC), high-energy Li metal (LiM) anode and Li-ion superionic halide solid electrolyte for application in electric vehicles and, especially in aircrafts. HELENA will support Europe, in this sense, on its transition towards a climate-neutral continent since electric aviation is poised to take off within the next five to 10 years, with innovations already being pursued for electric vehicle batteries. Moreover, HELENA will avoid dependence on Asia for battery production. HELENA is built by a multidisciplinary and highly research experienced consortium that covers the whole battery value chain and proposes a disruptive halide-based solid-state cell technology with the overall aim to significantly increase the adoption of these batteries on aircrafts and EVs The technical challenges that are presented by current conventional battery technology and the consumer needs will be overcome - especially the reduction in costs of battery devices, enable scalable and safe cell manufacturing, increasing their capabilities for long distance traveling and fast charging, ensuring a high safety of the battery.

objective_excerpt.en: Rhinoceros will develop, improve and demonstrate, in an industrially relevant environment, an economically and environmentally viable route for re-using, re-purposing, re-conditioning and recycling of EoL EV and stationary batteries. Rhinoceros will first develop a smart sorting and dismantling system enabling the automated classification and dismantling of LIBs and the reassembly of still working modules in new repurposed batteries for second life applications such as batteries for energy storage systems. When direct reuse and repurpose of batteries is not possible, a circular recycling route of all the materials present in LIBs (e.g., metals, graphite, fluorinated compounds and polymers, active materials) will be followed to close the materials loop. This route is based on a set of cost efficient, flexible and environmentally friendly routes targeting the pre-treatment, refining and the recovery of materials. Through product qualification by industrial end-users, Rhinoceros will demonstrate the direct production of high performances cathodic and anodic materials and other raw materials at competitive costs from battery recycling. The achievements will bring Europe to an increased independence level from foreigner manufacturers and raw materials suppliers.

summary.zh: PULSELiON：脉冲激光沉积固态电池制造。 联合体包括10个国家的14家机构，其中企业4家、高校及研究机构10家；欧盟最高资助额7.00百万欧元。
summary.en: Europe’s objective to have 30 million electric vehicles (EVs) by 2030 can only be achieved by large scale, in-house production of highly effective and performant batteries. objective_excerpt.en: Europe’s objective to have 30 million electric vehicles (EVs) by 2030 can only be achieved by large scale, in-house production of highly effective and performant batteries. Development of solid-state battery technologies could improve the energy density and safety of lithium metal solid state batteries. PULSELiON project aims to develop the manufacturing process of Gen 4b solid-state batteries (SSBs) based on lithium-metal anode, sulfide solid electrolytes, and Nickel-rich NMC cathode. Novel pulsed laser deposition technique developed by PULSEDEON will be adapted and modified into a single-step vacuum process for safe and efficient manufacturing of anode components composed of lithium metal, protective layers, and sulfide based solid electrolytes. The cathode layer will be made based on conventional wet processing techniques. Initially, the anode and cathode layers will be developed in small scale for making coin cells and monolayer cells for optimising the materials and process. SSB cells will be developed with optimised process routes and will be upscaled to a pilot line proof-of-concept (TRL 6) by manufacturing large scale solid-state batteries (10 Ah). Digitalisation will be incorporated in the process modelling task with the inputs obtained from process upscaling and cell testing tasks, which will enable efficient process optimisation.

This will allow to replace the flammable and unstable liquid electrolytes and enabling dendrite-free cyclingof high-energy lithium metal cells manufactured by sustainable processing. Special attention will be devoted to theoptimization of interfaces between the active material and polymer electrolyte. Materials selection will enable the useof the manufacturing technology available at BlueSolutions, which is readily scalable, based on sustainable processingusing solvent-free extrusion. PSIONIC is aiming to develop cells with a safety hazard level 2, since no liquid componentwill be in the cell at the end of the project.The research and innovation actions carried under the PSIONIC project will not only just contribute to the technologicaladvancements of all-solid-state Li-ion batteries in terms of safety, reliability, performance, cost, and sustainability, butwill also enable higher uptake by the electromobility sector and end consumers, paving a pathway towards climateneutrality, and green energy transition.

Regarding electrodes (i.e. anode and cathode) and electrolyte processing, innovative solvent-free extrusion routes, roll-to-roll approach and optimised solvent casting methods are suggested.SPINMATE’s Gen 4b SSB cells will create a new industry value chain in Europe towards their commercialisation. This new generation technology will ensure (i) enhanced energy densities, overcoming current LIB limitations, (ii) improved safety in both solutions and workers; (iii) increased sustainable mass production; and (iv) decreased carbon footprint and cost.

objective_excerpt.en: As of 2025, new generations of Li batteries based on silicon/carbon (Gen. 4a) and Li metal (Gen. 4b) anode, where flammable liquid electrolyte is replaced by a non-flammable solid-one, will take over the current Li-ion device. However, only all-solid-state Gen. 4b Li batteries are expected to fulfil the needed cell gravimetric energy density specifications demanded by electromobility and stationary applications. Therefore, SEATBELT ambition is to generate a local EU industry that revolves around a cost-effective, robust all-solid-state Li battery comprising sustainable materials by 2026. SEATBELT intends to achieve the first technological milestone of developing a battery cell (TRL5) meeting the needs of Electric Vehicle (EV) and stationary industry. The low-cost SEATBELT cell is safe-by-design with sustainable and recyclable materials, reaching high energy densities (>380 Wh/kg) and long cyclability (>500 cycles) by 2026 in line with the 2030 EU targets. The cells are produced by low-cost solvent-free extrusion process comprising a combination of innovative materials: thin Li metal, hybrid electrolyte, a safe cathode active material without critical materials and thin Al current collector. The cell design being optimized by interface (operando and atomistic modelling) and process (machine learning) methodologies. In addition, new in situ imaging instrumentation will be developed to investigate safety properties and mechanical deformation to assess cell safety in real conditions. An innovative recycling cycle from materials to cell level will be also established. Thus, SEATBELT will be the start point of a first EU all-solid-state battery value chain, whose main players in RTD and Industry sectors are within the consortium. So, cells and modules will cycle using industrially relevant protocols dedicated to EV and stationary applications. SEATBELT consortium is composed of 14 beneficiary partners and 3 affiliated entities, and one associated partner, from 7 European countries with an overall budget of 7851448.50€.

This will be further enabled by a specifically designed electrolyte to maximise the voltage window and enable stable SEI formation. A sustainable fibre based separator with superior safety features s in terms of thermal and mechanical stability will be developed. SiGNE will establish the viability of volume manufacturing with production quantities of battery components manufactured by project end.
